source.title: Vision Transformers provably learn spatial structure
source.authors: Samy Jelassi; M. E. Sander; Yuan-Fang Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation affecting the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: Studies learned spatial structure and test performance in simplified and image-trained Vision Transformers, including comparisons with convolutional models on permuted CIFAR-100; this is an extension to settings not specified in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, adaptive-optimizer comparisons, batch-size effects, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Its reported image results concern Vision Transformers, positional attention, and CNNs—not fully connected networks.
record.test_reason: The study investigates spatial structure learned by Vision Transformers and positional versus vanilla attention. None of V1–V8 is tested: in particular, the CNN comparisons use ViTs, not fully connected networks, so they do not test V3. Citations to optimizer, batch-size and dropout studies provide background rather than tests or operational uses of those findings.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but omits the theoretical transfer result: under the paper's synthetic assumptions, learned patch association enables sample-efficient transfer to a distribution sharing the same structure but potentially different features. The image experiments show learned associations after permutations and competitive positional-attention performance, including a 3.0 percentage-point ImageNet deficit. The authors explicitly limit their analysis to simplified positional attention and acknowledge that spatial-pattern recovery is distribution-dependent.
record.recipe_differences: The main theoretical results use a simplified single-head ViT with positional attention and a synthetic structured binary-classification distribution; image experiments use standard augmentations and AdamW. The paper does not reproduce the listed studies' interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: For CIFAR-100, CNN test performance changes with grid-shuffle size while ViT performance is described as unchanged. The authors report that the learned spatial grouping follows the inverse permutation.

fits_no_version.finding: A one-layer ViT achieves small test error on Gaussian inputs labeled by a cubic CNN without recovering the CNN's spatial grouping.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization by a ViT need not entail recovery of the labeling function's spatial grouping.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-100, ViT accuracy remains approximately unchanged across grid permutations, whereas ResNet-18 and VGG-19 accuracy depends on shuffle size; inverse permutation reveals learned local positional patterns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ViTs can learn spatial associations after fixed grid permutations and are less sensitive to these permutations than the tested CNNs.

fits_no_version.finding: Positional attention achieves 68.9% ImageNet accuracy versus 71.9% for vanilla ViT; the authors also describe competitive results on three smaller datasets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-independent positional attention can approach vanilla ViT accuracy in the tested image-classification recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 4.1–4.2 prove patch association and population accuracy at least 1−o(1) for the simplified ViT under the specified structured distribution, initialization and gradient-descent conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent can learn spatial associations while generalizing in a specified synthetic positional-attention model.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems 5.1–5.2 give polylogarithmic downstream sample requirements after learning shared spatial structure, versus a polynomial lower bound without knowledge of that structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned spatial associations can reduce downstream sample requirements when source and target distributions share their patch partition.

record.problems: Theory depends on a simplified positional-attention mechanism and a synthetic data distribution. Authors state that standard self-attention mixes data and positional encodings and that ViTs do not always learn the correct inductive bias. Several image-comparison values are only graphical; uncertainty/error bars are not included in the supplied figure descriptions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional result rows left out. Figure-only results for ViT accuracy on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and SVHN are retained as qualitative rows because the text explicitly says the models compete.

untested.parts: Joint demonstration of fitting fixed random labels, generalizing on natural labels, and chance-level held-out performance on random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
CNN versus fully connected image classifiers, including learned local connectivity and initialization from trained CNNs.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, and optimizer switching.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and changes to recipes that address large-batch penalties.
Controlled effects of adding or removing dropout, including training-set size, dropout strength and joint removal of weight decay.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, generalization-gap rankings, and comparisons with norm or margin measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because every row measures a different construct or architecture comparison; this does not imply the adjacent findings are unreadable or absent. No missing result bears on a listed version. Using Adam/AdamW, fixed batch sizes, or zero dropout without controlled comparisons does not test V4, V5 or V6.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and test performance on natural labels.
Width beyond the interpolation threshold and test error as width changes.
CNN versus fully connected networks and the effect of local connectivity relative to fully connected networks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across training-set sizes and configurations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
Removing highly memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: one-layer ViT
rows.stage_stated: trained from random initialization using gradient descent
rows.operation_detail: Trained with gradient descent on synthetic Gaussian data lacking spatial structure; evaluated test error and positional-encoding similarity.

conditions.value: synthetic Gaussian data; all patches i.i.d. standard Gaussian
label from a one-hidden-layer CNN with cubic activation

rows.measure: Test error and whether positional-encoding similarities match the convolution pattern.
rows.value: The ViT reaches small test error, but positional-encoding similarities do not match the convolution pattern.
rows.note: Authors describe the test error qualitatively; the figure plots its trajectory without a textual numeric value.
rows.check: Small test error without patch association measures neither random-label memorization nor any other listed version. Split test error and positional-pattern recovery if retaining these as adjacent findings; 'partial' has no applicable claim referent.

rows.subject: ViT
rows.size_stated: 7 layers, 12 heads, hidden and MLP dimension 384
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-100 with shuffled image grids; evaluated test accuracy and learned positional similarities.
rows.measure: Test accuracy and recovery of spatially localized patterns after applying the inverse permutation.
rows.baseline: Original CIFAR-100 test accuracy; figure only.
rows.value: Permuted and original test accuracy are described as equal; inverse permutation recovers spatially localized patterns.
rows.note: Accuracy values are presented graphically; the text states the ViT performs equally on permuted and original data.
rows.check: ViT permutation robustness and spatial-pattern recovery do not test V3's CNN-versus-fully-connected comparison. Accuracy is reported across shuffle sizes 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32; the inverse-permutation visualization specifically uses shuffle size 2. Separate those measures and conditions.

relation.reason: The study discusses generalization and implicit regularization without testing or using a listed claim version.

tranche.reason: The study tests patch association and transfer in ViTs, not V1–V8. Its CNN comparisons use ViTs rather than fully connected networks and therefore do not test V3.

source_check.notes: Training details conflict: Section 6 gives 300 epochs, AdamW and 5 seeds; Appendix A.1 gives 200 epochs and Adam for small datasets; Figure 7 explicitly gives 10 seeds. The theoretical transfer result concerns shared spatial structure with potentially different features.
